category_title: Students with ASD and profound hearing loss exhibiting escape-motivated tantrums during academic tasks
minimal_context: Charlie is sitting at a table in his classroom during reading class and is asked to read a paragraph from a book aloud.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Charlie, it is time for our reading lesson. Please look at this book and read the first paragraph aloud.

STUDENT: (Pushes the book away and shakes his head to refuse to work)

TUTOR: We need to do our reading work now. Please start reading.

STUDENT: (Starts to melt down, whining and engaging in avoidance behaviors by turning his body away from the reading material)

TUTOR: Charlie, you need to stay at the table and finish this assignment.

STUDENT: (Screams loudly, pounds his fist on the table, and leaves his chair to escape the reading work)

options.A: Allow Charlie to call on a neighbor, ask a friend, or poll the rest of the class for help with reading the assigned paragraph.
options.B: Use a firm command to maintain classroom order during the reading lesson, such as telling the students to make no noise.
options.C: Allow Charlie to select a positive reinforcer before beginning the reading, which he earns when he finishes the paragraph or makes an honest attempt.
options.D: Give Charlie the opportunity to communicate his knowledge of the reading assignment through alternative methods like drawing, acting, or speaking.
